introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 2 (0560), Paper 2 - Modern World History Since 1870, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions. TWO questions must be chosen from SECTION A, ONE from SECTION B and ONE other from SECTION C. One of the two questions chosen from SECTION A must be a Starred question.

Maps should be used to illustrate answers where appropriate. All questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION A: CAMEROON SINCE 1850**

Question ONE is compulsory. Answer either 1A* or 1B* and one other Question from this section.

**1. Either**

**A\* (Starred question)** *Study this extract bearing on the scramble for the Cameroon in the 1880s and answer questions (a) to (d) which follow. (The maximum mark for each sub-question is indicated in brackets).*

*(The extract is set line by line as printed; the line numbers printed in the right margin are shown in square brackets.)*

> The ultimate result of the race for the annexation of Cameroon was the signing of the  
> Germano-Duala treaty... Kings Bell and Akwa signed for Cameroon while German traders  
> signed for their home government. Since the next day was a Sunday and therefore a non-  
> working day, official celebrations marking the German annexation were pushed forward to  
> Monday July 14th. On this day the imperial German Commissioner solemnly hoisted the [5]  
> German flag over Douala  
> News of the German annexation of Cameroon came as a complete surprise to observers in  
> Britain, and sparked off a chain of reactions within Cameroon, Britain and elsewhere. The  
> British government condemned the German move, accusing Germany of staging a coup in  
> Cameroon. In the meantime, Consul Hewett, who arrived too late, rushed to Ambas Bay [10]  
> and on the 19th July 1884 proclaimed Ambas Bay a British Settlement. Two Poles and other  
> pro-British agents embarked on a treaty-signing spree... In the process, these British agents  
> acquired territories on the foot of the Cameroon mountain for Britain. The aim was to  
> confine the Germans to the small coastal strip around Douala. British warships continued to  
> patrol the Cameroon coast but refused to salute the German flag. [15]  
> It was a fascinating story of bribes exchanging hands such as rum, schnapps, whisky,  
> tobacco, cloth, brandy and dem-Johnny whisky.  
> These anti German activities by Pro-British agents along the Cameroon coast alarmed the  
> Germans. The German Chancellor at the time was furious. He warned that the land  
> grabbing activities of British agents along the Cameroon coast was indeed an unfriendly act [20]  
> that would not be accepted.  
> Anglo German relations, however, witnessed a marked improvement in 1887 when the  
> British government refused to validate treaties signed on her behalf along the Cameroon  
> coast. Territories that had been acquired as a result of such treaties were ceded to Germany.  
> The peaceful resolution of the Anglo-German dispute over Cameroon encouraged German [25]  
> missionaries and explorers to embark on the penetration of the Cameroon interior. In 1889,  
> the first German station was set up and in 1891,a landmark treaty was signed between a  
> German explorer and the Fon of Bali.

**Source:** *Cited in ABBIA, 29-30 (1975) pp.165-171.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a)

(i) State both the month and the year the Germano-Duala treaty was signed as mentioned in line 2 of the extract.

(ii) Write down the name of **two** German traders who signed the treaty mentioned in a (i) above.

(iii) Who was the German Imperial Commissioner who hoisted the German flag over Douala as indicated in the extract (line 5)?

**(2+2+1 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Month and year of the treaty (2 marks).** The Germano-Duala treaty was signed in **July 1884** (on Saturday 12 July 1884). The extract fixes the date indirectly: the official celebrations were "pushed forward to Monday July 14th" because the day after the signing was a Sunday, so the treaty was signed on the Saturday before, 12 July. (1 mark for the month, July; 1 mark for the year, 1884.)

**(ii) Two German traders (2 marks).** Any two of the following names (1 mark each):
- **Eduard Schmidt**, the agent of the Woermann firm of Hamburg;
- **Johannes Voss**, the agent of the firm Jantzen and Thormählen.

(The treaty was signed on the Cameroonian side by Kings Bell and Akwa. The German traders signed for their firms and, as the extract says, "for their home government".)

**(iii) The Imperial Commissioner (1 mark).** **Dr Gustav Nachtigal**, the German explorer who had been appointed Imperial Commissioner for West Africa. He arrived at Douala on 11 July 1884, after having first signed a treaty in Togo, and he hoisted the German flag over Douala on 14 July 1884.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b)

(i) Name the Douala Chief and the town that reacted angrily to the hoisting of the German flag over Douala mentioned in a (iii) above.

(ii) In which of the towns along the coast were the British forced to hoist their own flag?

(iii) In what year did the British pull down their flag over the town mentioned in b (ii) above?

**(2+1+1 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) The chief and his town (2 marks).** The chief was **Lock Priso** (Priso Bele Dibobe, called "King Joss" by the traders) and his town was **Hickory Town (Bonaberi)**, on the left bank of the Wouri river. He refused to accept the treaty signed by Kings Bell and Akwa and the German annexation, and he resisted. (1 mark for the chief, 1 mark for the town.) In December 1884 the Germans punished the resistance by bombarding and burning Hickory Town.

**(ii) The town where the British hoisted their flag (1 mark).** **Ambas Bay** (the area of the present Limbe, then Victoria). The extract says that Consul Hewett, who arrived too late at Douala, "rushed to Ambas Bay" and proclaimed it a British Settlement on 19 July 1884. The British were forced to fall back on Ambas Bay because the Germans had already annexed Douala and its neighbourhood.

**(iii) The year the flag was pulled down (1 mark).** **1887.** As the extract says, in 1887 the British government refused to validate the treaties signed on its behalf along the coast, and the territories acquired by such treaties, Ambas Bay included, were ceded to Germany.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c)

(i) Which international treaty of the 1880s signed between Britain and Germany caused her to hand over territories she had acquired along the Cameroon coast to Germany?

(ii) **When** and **where** was the first German station established in the territory of Cameroon as indicated in the extract (line 27)?

(iii) Name any **one** of the German missionary bodies that was encouraged to operate in Cameroon as mentioned in line 26.

(iv) Give the name of the German explorer and the inland station he established in 1891 (line 28).

**(1+2+1+2 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) The treaty (1 mark).** The **Anglo-German Treaty (Agreement) of 1886**, by which Britain recognised the German hold on the Douala coast and the surrounding area. It was followed in **1887** by the cession of Ambas Bay and the other coastal territories acquired by the British treaties, as the extract says.

**(ii) The first German station (2 marks).** It was set up in **1889** (1 mark) at **Barombi** (Barombi Station, near Lake Barombi in the Kumba area), founded by the explorer Eugen Zintgraff (1 mark).

**(iii) A German missionary body (1 mark).** Any one of: the **Basel Mission** (which began in Cameroon in 1886, taking over from the British Baptists), the **Pallottine Fathers** (German Catholic mission, from 1890), or the **German Baptist mission** (from the early 1890s).

**(iv) The explorer and the inland station (2 marks).** The explorer was **Eugen Zintgraff** (1 mark), who founded **Bali Station** in the Grassfields in 1891 after signing a treaty with the Fon of Bali, Galega I (1 mark).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) What benefits did the Bali people derive from the **landmark** treaty they signed with the Germans?

**(5 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
The treaty of 1891 was a treaty of friendship between the German explorer Eugen Zintgraff and the Fon of Bali (Bali-Nyonga), Galega I. It brought the Bali people the following benefits (any five well explained points, 1 mark each):

1. **Military protection and weapons.** The Germans supplied guns and ammunition and promised protection, which strengthened Bali against its enemies and neighbours such as Bafut and the other chiefdoms of the Grassfields.
2. **Territorial expansion and political power.** With German support the Bali extended their control over weaker neighbouring chiefdoms and were treated by the Germans as the leading power and chief ally in the Grassfields. The Fon of Bali was favoured and recognised by the German administration.
3. **Trade and wealth.** Bali Station gave the Bali access to European goods (cloth, salt, guns, tools) and the Bali acted as middlemen, carriers and traders between the Germans and the interior, earning wages and profits.
4. **Employment.** Many Bali served as porters, soldiers and labourers in the German stations and expeditions, and earned wages.
5. **Peace and security.** The alliance reduced the danger of attack and raids on Bali itself.
6. **Education and Christianity.** Later, with the support of the German authorities, the Basel Mission opened its station and schools in Bali (in the early 1900s), and Bali became one of the early centres of western education and of Christianity in the Grassfields.
7. **Prestige of the Fon.** The Fon's authority and prestige grew, and he was strengthened by the German alliance.

In return the Bali had to accept German authority, supply labour and carriers and help in the German military expeditions, and Bali later lost part of its independence.
